style: Spoken English voices, British accents, no singing. Yorkshire woman paramedic, hoarse, breathless, shouting; Mancunian man paramedic, gruff Manchester voice, talking over her; West Midlands Brummie driver bellowing over a wailing siren. Then a different world: an elderly upper-class English gentleman, cut-glass Received Pronunciation, deep bored baritone, clipped and petulant, muffled behind a thick car window. Underscore of a BBC Sunday-night hospital drama: frantic chamber-string ostinato, low synth pulse at heartbeat tempo, rain, heart monitor beeping faster. Strings stop dead at a red light, leaving rain and an idling engine. Under the posh man, one thin sustained high violin note only. Ends on a flat continuous monitor tone, then silence.
exclude: American accent, singing, sung melody, chorus, rap, choir, backing vocals, drum kit, beat, pop, comedy, upbeat, autotune
lyrics:
[Intro: siren, rain, racing strings, fast monitor beeps]

[Spoken, shouted. Paramedic Shirley, Yorkshire woman, hoarse]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!

[Spoken, over her. Paramedic Gaz, Mancunian man, gruff]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!

[Spoken, bellowed over the siren. Driver Dean, Brummie]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!

[Strings cut dead. Rain, idling engine]

[Spoken. Gaz]
Why have we stopped?!

[One thin high violin note. Muffled behind glass. Sir Rupert, elderly posh English gentleman, bored]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!

[Spoken, quiet. Shirley]
Fifty over twen—

[Flatline tone]

[Silence]

[End]
